Have you ever wondered why happiness sometimes feels just out of reach, almost like you're chasing it around a corner?
Welcome—let's take this journey together, exploring what it really means to make happiness happen in our lives.
In Lucky Go Happy: Make Happiness Happen!, Paul Van Der Merwe invites us to look at happiness from a fresh perspective. He asks us to think about luck, choice, and how much control we actually have over our own joy.
Is happiness just a matter of chance, or is there something more to it? What if we could actually shape our happiness, no matter what life throws at us?
As we move forward, we'll dive into inspiring stories and down-to-earth strategies that light the way toward a more joyful life. You'll see that happiness isn't some far-off destination—it's woven into the choices we make every single day.
Through small shifts in the way we think and act, even ordinary moments can become bright spots of real fulfillment.
So, get ready to discover how happiness can be learned, practiced, and celebrated—by all of us, together. There's a whole world of meaning and delight waiting, and we're about to set out on this adventure side by side.

Let's kick things off with Chapter 1: Understanding Happiness as a Personal Choice, Not a Matter of Luck.
Have you ever caught yourself thinking that happiness just sort of happens to some people? That it’s the result of good fortune, or something that comes along when life finally lines up the way you want?
Here’s the truth: happiness isn’t a prize for the lucky. It’s something you create, step by step, through your own decisions and actions.
Think about it this way—imagine happiness as a garden. A beautiful garden doesn’t just spring up overnight or appear by accident, does it? No, it takes planting, watering, and a whole lot of care. If you simply wait for flowers to bloom without ever planting a seed, you’ll be staring at empty soil for a long time.
The same goes for happiness. If you wait for the perfect conditions, or hope that luck will drop joy into your lap, you’re putting your happiness in someone else’s hands—or leaving it up to chance. But when you choose to nurture your own sense of well-being, when you take small, intentional steps, that’s when your life starts to bloom.
Now, don’t get me wrong—luck can play a part in what happens to us. Life is full of surprises, both good and bad. But luck isn’t the architect of your happiness. What really matters is the choices you make in response to what life throws your way.
Think about two people who lose their jobs on the same day. One might sink into frustration, seeing only misfortune. The other could treat it as a turning point—a chance to learn, stretch, and maybe even try something new. The event is the same, but their responses are worlds apart.
So, what’s the big idea here? Let’s boil it down:
Happiness is the result of intentional action, not random luck.
Your personal choices shape your happiness far more than anything happening on the outside.
And when you respond proactively to life’s challenges, you open up space for growth and real fulfillment.
If you take just one thing from this chapter, let it be this: happiness isn’t something you wait for—it’s something you build, one choice at a time.
By shifting your mindset from passive to active, you’re laying the foundation for a more joyful, meaningful life. And that’s where your journey really begins.

Chapter Two: Taking Initiative and Embracing Responsibility for Change.
Once you realize that happiness really is a personal responsibility, what comes next? Well, it’s all about taking initiative. Instead of just hoping things will get better, you start actively engaging with life and all the possibilities it offers.
A lot of us reach moments where we feel stuck—like we’re waiting for something outside of ourselves to shift before we can be truly happy. But here’s the thing: if you’re always waiting for circumstances to change, you might end up feeling frustrated and stuck in place.
Taking initiative means being willing to step forward, even when you can’t see exactly where the path leads. Think of it like setting sail on a wide, unpredictable ocean. Sure, you can’t control the winds or the tides, but you always have the choice to raise the anchor and set your own course.
So, where do you start? Try looking at the parts of your life that feel unsatisfying or where you’re longing for something more. Instead of treating these feelings as permanent, see them as invitations to take action.
For example, if your job leaves you feeling empty, maybe it’s time to learn a new skill, look for a mentor, or volunteer for projects that excite you. The most important thing is to stop just wishing for things to be different and start taking real, concrete steps—even if they’re small.
Here’s a simple framework that can guide you:
First, recognize where you want change.
Second, accept that it’s up to you to start that change.
Third, break big goals into smaller, doable actions.
And finally, keep going—even when things get tough or uncertain.
Now, taking initiative doesn’t mean you’ll succeed overnight. But it does get things moving. Each small step you take builds your confidence, and opens doors you didn’t even know were there. Before you know it, you’re moving from just waiting around to really participating in your own life.
And hey, let’s be honest—taking initiative can feel scary. The fear of messing up, or worrying about what others might think, can make you want to stand still. But more often than not, those fears shrink the moment you take action. Even if things aren’t perfect, the simple act of moving forward gives you a sense of control and hope.
Think about someone who’s felt lonely for years, and finally decides to join a local club or reconnect with an old friend. That first step might feel awkward, but it starts a chain reaction—new connections, new experiences, and, eventually, more happiness and fulfillment.
When you embrace responsibility and start taking initiative, you’re claiming your power to shape your own life. It’s not about trying to control every single outcome. It’s about choosing to show up, and play an active role in your own story as it unfolds.

Let’s dive into Chapter 3: Learning from Setbacks and Turning Challenges into Growth.
You know, no journey toward happiness is ever completely smooth. We all face obstacles—setbacks, disappointments, even failures. But here’s the thing: what really sets people apart isn’t a life without hardship, but how they turn adversity into an opportunity for growth.
Think of challenges as teachers. They offer lessons you just can’t get when everything’s easy and comfortable. When life gets tough, it’s totally normal to want to pull back or feel discouraged. But what if you could see those setbacks as stepping stones—moments that actually help you become stronger and wiser?
Imagine a river slowly carving its way through solid rock. Over time, that steady flow shapes the landscape, creating canyons and valleys. In the same way, when you keep learning from challenges, your character gets shaped, and your understanding of yourself and the world deepens.
So, how do you actually learn from setbacks in a way that leads to real growth? Let’s break it down:
Acknowledge the difficulty—don’t pretend it’s not there, and don’t blame yourself or others. Reflect on what the experience is trying to teach you. Identify what you could change or improve for next time. And most importantly, keep going—even when it’s uncomfortable. Trust that you really can grow from this.
Let’s make it real. Say you’ve just wrapped up a project at work, and it didn’t go well. Maybe you feel embarrassed or frustrated. Instead of giving up, what if you paused to reflect? Maybe you’ll notice you needed more preparation, or that communication could’ve been better. Armed with that insight, you approach the next project differently—more skilled, more confident.
The point isn’t to be perfect. It’s about progress. Every challenge you face and work through builds resilience—that inner strength that helps you bounce back and adapt. Over time, this resilience becomes your superpower, letting you face new difficulties with more courage and optimism.
Here’s something to pay attention to along the way: self-compassion. When you’re struggling, being harsh on yourself only makes it harder to learn. But if you treat yourself with a little kindness and understanding, it becomes much easier to move forward.
Picture this in daily life: you have a disagreement with a friend. Instead of just blaming them or beating yourself up, you reflect on your own role. You learn from it, repair the relationship, and next time, you avoid the same misunderstanding.
So, here’s the key takeaway—when you learn from setbacks, you turn challenges from painful roadblocks into real opportunities for personal growth. This mindset not only helps you find more happiness, but also brings a deeper sense of purpose and meaning to your life.

Let’s dive into Chapter 4: “Cultivating Attitude, Gratitude, and Resilience for Lasting Happiness.”
Now that you’ve got a foundation of personal responsibility and a growth mindset, what comes next? Well, it’s all about building the qualities that keep happiness going, no matter what life throws your way. And you’ll find three essentials at the heart of lasting well-being: attitude, gratitude, and resilience.
Think about attitude for a second. The way you look at situations—how you interpret what’s happening around you—shapes everything. Having a positive, hopeful outlook doesn’t mean pretending problems don’t exist. It’s more about choosing to focus on what’s possible and where you can make a difference. Imagine slipping on a pair of glasses that filter the world through optimism. Suddenly, you spot opportunities you might have missed and notice those small, everyday joys.
Gratitude comes next. This is really about pausing to notice and appreciate the good stuff—even when things are tough. Instead of zeroing in on what’s missing, you shift your attention to what’s already there. It could be as simple as savoring a warm meal, hearing a kind word, or catching a beautiful sunset. Just taking a moment each day to reflect on something that brings you comfort or joy can make a big difference.
And then there’s resilience—the ability to bounce back from setbacks and adapt when things change. Resilience isn’t about avoiding pain or hardship. Instead, it’s about having the strength to keep moving forward, learning and growing from every challenge you face. Each time you overcome something tough, you’re building up this inner muscle.
So, how can you actually nurture these qualities? Let’s break it down with a few simple practices:
Start your day with a positive intention or affirmation. This could be something like, “Today, I’ll focus on learning,” or, “I’ll look for the bright spots.”
Keep a gratitude journal. Jot down the small and big things you’re thankful for—maybe three things at the end of each day.
Take care of yourself and reach out for support when it’s tough. Self-care really matters, and it’s okay to lean on others.
Reflect on past challenges and notice how far you’ve come, how much you’ve grown, and the strengths you’ve discovered along the way.
Let’s say you’re having a stressful time at work. You might begin your morning by setting a positive intention—like focusing on learning or being there for your team. When the day winds down, you write down three things you’re grateful for. This simple routine helps you balance out the stress and reminds you of what’s good.
As you keep up these habits, you’re actually building a solid base for your happiness. Attitude, gratitude, and resilience start to work together, lifting each other up. Feeling grateful makes it easier to stay positive, and resilience gives you the strength to stick with it—especially when life gets rough.
You’ve probably seen this in people who seem to shine, even during hard times. They hold onto hope and purpose, and somehow, they still find things to be thankful for. Their ability to find meaning, even when things are tough, is a powerful reminder of what’s possible for any of us.
So, here’s the key takeaway: By practicing attitude, gratitude, and resilience, you’re setting yourself up for lasting happiness. These aren’t just traits you’re born with—they’re skills you can build and strengthen over time. With a little practice, they’ll become your steady companions on the journey to a more joyful, fulfilling life.

Chapter 5: Discovering Purpose and Finding Fulfillment Through Helping Others
As you dive deeper into what happiness really means, you start to notice something important. True fulfillment? It isn’t just about chasing your own dreams or adding up personal wins. Real, lasting happiness often shows up when you find a sense of purpose—and when you use that purpose to help other people.
Sure, personal achievements and little pleasures can give you a quick shot of satisfaction. But have you ever noticed how those moments tend to fade? In contrast, when your life is guided by meaning and service—when you're doing things that matter, not just to you but to others—it creates a much deeper, steady kind of contentment.
Think of purpose like your own guiding star. It gives you direction, a sense that your life fits together and really means something. And here’s the thing: purpose doesn’t have to be some huge, world-changing goal. Sometimes, it’s found in the everyday—a kind gesture, meaningful work, or simply showing up for the people around you. What matters most is living in a way that matches your values, and looking for those moments where you can make a positive difference, no matter how small.
Helping others just naturally grows out of this sense of purpose. When you give—whether it’s your time, your attention, or your support—you’re not just making someone else’s day brighter. You’re also enriching your own life. It creates this beautiful cycle where giving and receiving are constantly connected.
So, how do you actually discover your purpose and start making a difference? Here are a few practical steps you might try:
First, take some time to reflect on your strengths, your values, and what truly excites you.
Then, look for ways you can use those strengths to serve others—maybe through your job, your community, or even small acts of kindness.
Don’t forget about those little moments: holding the door, offering encouragement, or just listening when someone needs it. Those all count.
And finally, try to build genuine connections with people by showing empathy and support.
Let’s make it real. Maybe you love teaching—so you volunteer to mentor young people. Or you’re passionate about art, and you use your creativity to lift someone’s spirits in your neighborhood. The specific way you help? That’s less important than the intention and care you bring to it.
Here’s something else to keep in mind: having a sense of purpose and helping others can actually help you weather life’s ups and downs. When things get tough, meaning gives you motivation and hope. Knowing that what you do matters, and that you’re part of something bigger, can make all the difference.
In daily life, this might be as simple as checking in on a neighbor, or being the teammate who always has a listening ear. These gestures may seem small, but they ripple outward, spreading positivity and connection in ways you might never fully see.
So, what’s the big takeaway? Chasing happiness isn’t just a solo journey. When you discover your purpose and reach out to help others, you find a kind of fulfillment that lasts—something that goes far beyond quick bursts of pleasure. That sense of meaning becomes the foundation for a happy life that’s deep, strong, and truly resilient.

Chapter 6: Building Supportive Relationships and Community.
Once you’ve got a sense of purpose and you’re in the habit of helping others, there’s another piece that really matters—relationships.
People are wired to connect. Our happiness is tied so closely to the quality of our relationships, whether that’s with friends, family, or even our wider community.
Think of your relationships like the roots of a big tree. Those roots keep the tree anchored and nourished, right? In the same way, strong, healthy relationships help keep us steady and grounded—especially when life gets stormy.
So, how do you actually build supportive connections? It starts with intention. Here are a few things you can do:
Make time for the people who matter to you. Don’t just let those relationships run on autopilot.
Practice really listening, and show empathy—even when it’s hard.
Let people know you appreciate them. A simple “thank you” or a warm gesture goes a long way.
And when conflict pops up, try to meet it with honesty and kindness.
Imagine you set aside a little time each week to check in with friends or family. You’re not just catching up—you’re making space for real, meaningful conversations. And if you ever hit a misunderstanding, what if you approached it with curiosity instead of frustration? You might just turn a disagreement into a deeper connection.
Now, let’s zoom out a bit. Community takes these ideas and expands them beyond individual relationships. Being part of a group—maybe it’s your neighborhood, your workplace, or a hobby club—gives you a sense of belonging and shared purpose.
When you join in on group activities, volunteer, or even just show up to support a neighbor, you’re weaving yourself into the fabric of something bigger. These small acts build trust and connection, not just for you, but for everyone involved.
Picture yourself joining a local club, or attending a community event, or maybe helping out when someone nearby needs a hand. That’s how you strengthen the ties that hold a community together.
At the end of the day, supportive relationships and a strong sense of community aren’t just nice to have—they’re essential for a happy, meaningful life.
When you invest in these connections, you build a network of care that can help you weather life’s challenges and celebrate its joys.

Chapter 7: Practicing Mindfulness and Presence in Daily Life
As we’ve talked about relationships and community as powerful sources of support, there’s another anchor you can rely on—one that comes from within. That’s mindfulness. So, what is it really? Mindfulness is all about paying attention to the present moment, with a real sense of openness and curiosity. It means being fully engaged with what’s happening right now, instead of getting caught up in regrets about the past or worries about what’s coming next.
Picture your mind as a busy train station. Thoughts and emotions are like trains, constantly arriving and leaving. Practicing mindfulness is like stepping onto the platform and simply watching those trains go by, instead of jumping onto every single one. This gentle awareness gives you a little breathing room—and the freedom to choose how you want to respond, rather than just react.
So how can you bring more mindfulness into your day? Here are a few approachable ways:
Try setting aside just a few minutes for quiet reflection or meditation each day. Notice the sensations in your body, your thoughts, and your feelings—without judging them. Bring your full attention to simple things, like eating a meal or taking a walk. And when stress starts to creep in, pause for a moment and take a few deep breaths.
Let’s make this real. Imagine starting your morning by sitting quietly, tuning in to the natural rhythm of your breath and the feeling of your body. Or maybe, as you go through your day, you focus all your attention on a conversation with a friend, or truly savor the taste of lunch. These moments of presence add up.
Here’s something to remember: mindfulness isn’t about reaching some perfect state. It’s about coming back to the present, again and again. Over time, this habit can actually make you more resilient to stress, and open you up to more joy. It even helps your relationships—because when you’re fully present with someone, real connection happens.
And in everyday life, mindfulness can help you break those cycles of rumination and worry. Say you’re hit with a tough emotion; if you pause, notice, and name what you’re feeling, it can actually take away some of its sting and help you choose a wiser next step.
By making mindfulness a part of your routine, you’re building a foundation for happiness that’s steady and strong. You’ll find more to appreciate in life’s little moments, and you’ll make choices that really line up with your values.
So, why not start small, and see how much brighter your days can feel?

prosody.p: Chapter Eight—Managing Expectations and Letting Go of Perfectionism.

Let’s take a closer look at something that holds so many of us back from real happiness: the habit of setting sky-high expectations and chasing perfection. Have you ever noticed how easy it is to feel let down—not just by others, but by yourself, or even life itself? It’s like we’re all wearing these invisible glasses that make us focus only on what’s missing or what could’ve been better.

Imagine expectations as the lenses you use to see the world. Now, when those lenses are fogged up with perfectionism, even truly beautiful moments can suddenly look flawed. But what if you could wipe those lenses clean? By adjusting your expectations—making them a bit more realistic and a whole lot more compassionate—you start to notice the richness and beauty that’s already there.
So, how do you actually do this? Here are a few strategies that can help:
First, set goals that stretch you, but that you can actually reach. It’s great to aim high—but not so high that you’re always out of reach.
Second, remind yourself that mistakes and setbacks aren’t failures—they’re just part of how we grow. Really, who learns anything by getting it perfect the first time?
Next, try to celebrate your progress along the way—not just the final outcome. Every small step forward is worth some recognition.
And maybe most important, practice being kind to yourself when things don’t go as planned. Self-compassion is a powerful antidote to perfectionism.

Let’s put this into a real-world example. Think about a parent who’s feeling the pressure to pull off the perfect holiday for their family. It’s so easy to get wrapped up in flawless details, but what really matters? When you focus on simply enjoying time together—the laughter, the traditions, even the little mishaps—you create the memories that last. The perfect holiday isn’t about everything going smoothly, but about truly being present.

Letting go of perfectionism also means being willing to show up as your real, sometimes imperfect self. That kind of vulnerability is what makes it possible to connect with others on a deeper level. When you’re open about your struggles, or when you ask for help, you’re actually inviting others in—and that builds true belonging.

Picture a student who’s just received a disappointing grade. Instead of spiraling into self-criticism, they take a breath and look for what they’ve learned. By shifting their expectations and practicing a little self-kindness, they find the motivation to keep going—maybe even stronger than before.

So, here’s the key takeaway: when you manage your expectations and let go of perfectionism, you make space for real happiness. You start to appreciate yourself—and your life—as it is, instead of chasing some impossible ideal. That’s the kind of freedom that lets you truly enjoy the journey.

Chapter 9: Creating Daily Rituals and Habits That Support Well-Being.
If you want happiness to last, it takes more than a burst of effort here and there. True well-being is built on the small things you do every single day—those rituals and habits that give your life rhythm, stability, and meaning.
Imagine your habits as the bricks that build your house of happiness. Each positive habit—even if it seems tiny—adds strength and structure. Over time, as you keep laying those bricks, they form a solid foundation for your well-being.
So, how do you actually build supportive habits? Here are a few simple steps:
First, pick one or two small actions that truly fit your values. Maybe it’s something as simple as a daily walk, jotting down a note of gratitude before bed, or carving out a few minutes for creative expression.
Next, weave those actions into your daily routine, making them part of your regular rhythm.
Track your progress and celebrate your consistency—even if the results seem small at first. Remember, it’s not about instant transformation, but about showing up for yourself again and again.
And when life changes, don’t be afraid to adjust your habits to fit your new reality. Flexibility is just as important as consistency.
The beauty of rituals is that they don’t have to be complicated. Their real power comes from being intentional and showing up every day. Over time, these habits start to run automatically, which means you don’t have to rely on willpower alone—especially when life gets busy or stressful.
Picture a family gathering for dinner each night, sharing stories and building connection. Or someone who starts every workday with a few moments of mindful breathing to set a calm, focused tone.
These small acts, when done regularly, add up. They shape the way you experience life, making space for happiness to grow.
So, here’s the key takeaway: by creating daily rituals and habits that support your well-being, you’re not just making positive choices—you’re building an environment where happiness can truly flourish.

Let’s talk about Chapter 10: Embracing Change and Navigating Life’s Transitions.
So here we are, at the final step in the framework—learning how to embrace change, and handle life’s inevitable transitions with a little more grace.
You know, change is just part of being alive. Relationships shift, careers take new turns, our health ebbs and flows, and circumstances can flip upside down when we least expect it.
Sure, change can be a little unsettling. But it also brings new chances to grow and start fresh.
Imagine your life as a river, always moving, always reshaping its path. If you try to fight the current, you’ll struggle. But when you learn to go with the flow, you give yourself room to adapt and discover something new.
So, how do you actually embrace change, instead of dreading it? Here are a few practical ideas:
First, it helps to acknowledge any feelings of uncertainty or loss—without judging yourself. It’s okay to feel a little off-balance.
Next, look for meaning or opportunity in whatever’s new. Sometimes, the biggest surprises turn out to be the most valuable.
Stay rooted in your core values and lean on your support network. Whether that’s family, friends, or even a favorite hobby, these anchors help you stay steady.
And don’t forget to give yourself time to adjust. Self-care matters, especially during big transitions.
Let me give you a real-life example. Picture someone facing retirement. At first, they might feel anxious or even a little lost. But by diving into new interests, reconnecting with loved ones, and really thinking about what matters most, they can turn that blank slate into a brand new, joyful chapter.
Navigating change is also about letting go—releasing old habits, identities, or relationships that no longer fit. That can be bittersweet, but it makes space for new growth and opportunities.
Think about a family moving to a new city. At first, everything feels unfamiliar, but as they make new friends and create routines, that strange place starts to feel like home.
Or maybe you’re stepping into a new role at work. Sure, it’s a little intimidating, but by looking for ways to learn and connect, you’ll find your rhythm.
Here’s the key takeaway: When you approach change with openness and resilience, you turn those tough transitions into opportunities for renewal. Flexibility is what keeps happiness lasting, because it lets you keep growing and adapting—no matter what life brings.

As we wrap up, let’s take a moment to really bring all these ideas together. You know, happiness isn’t about making one big leap—it’s about taking small, thoughtful steps, day after day. Every principle we’ve talked about—choosing happiness, taking initiative, learning from your setbacks, building gratitude and resilience, finding your sense of purpose, nurturing relationships, practicing mindfulness, managing expectations, creating good habits, and rolling with change—they all fit together, like pieces of a bigger puzzle. When you put them all in place, they create a life that’s more joyful, more meaningful, and a whole lot more fulfilling.
Here’s what really stands out:
Happiness doesn’t just show up—you grow it, choice by choice, moment by moment. When you take initiative and own your path, you open up new doors for growth. And when you hit bumps in the road, those setbacks? They’re not dead ends—they’re actually some of your best teachers, helping you build resilience and wisdom along the way.
Remember, the people around you matter. Supportive relationships and a sense of community are essential ingredients for lasting well-being. And it’s those daily habits—being mindful, keeping your expectations realistic, and making small positive changes—that keep your happiness alive over the long haul.
So, as you reflect on these steps, keep this in mind: happiness isn’t a finish line you cross once—it’s the way you move through life, in all its ups and downs. There will be days that feel easy, and others that challenge you. But what counts most is your willingness to come back, again and again, to the practices and mindsets that help you thrive.
You don’t have to do everything at once. Just start with what feels doable today—a quick note of gratitude, a mindful breath, or reaching out to someone you care about. Over time, these little choices add up, and you’ll find your life feeling more connected, more purposeful, and more alive.
And above all, be gentle with yourself. The path to happiness isn’t a straight line, and setbacks are just part of the journey. Every single day offers you a new chance to plant those seeds of intention, to nurture the garden of your life, and to discover meaning in both the ordinary and the extraordinary. With patience, self-compassion, and a curious spirit, you really can create a life that’s not just happier, but richer—and truly your own.
